summary.intent: Drive the caliper repo's remaining trails (153–158) to completion by delegating to sub-agents: publish the Callisto release flow (GitHub Releases, attested binaries, recovery), keep commits signed, and answer side questions about trail rendering and the macOS 14 runner retirement.
summary.outcome: Trail 158 was pushed as three stacked PRs (#286–#288) and merged by the user; stranded commits from #281/#283 were re-landed via #289/#290, and two workers were started on trails 155–156 (detection stack) and 157 (trust). Trail bodies were rewritten without tables and the macOS 14 question was resolved as no action needed.

repo: Callisto 0.16.0 hard-codes the attesting workflow path as .github/workflows/callisto-release.yml (RELEASE_COORDINATOR_WORKFLOW_PATH), so release.yml had to be renamed; verification fails with E140 otherwise.
The `[release]` section in callisto.toml requires `github-release` on the product package (E197), so GitHub Releases must land before binaries/attestations.
The Homebrew tap keys on tags (npm/caliper-docgen@x.y.z via livecheck), not Releases; tag names were left unchanged. The tap lives in another repo and was not inspected.

Enabling github-release makes 0.9.0 look unfinished to `callisto release pending`; without `--from` it stops with E166, so RELEASE_PENDING_FROM is pinned to 2daef927 (0.9.0 release commit). The first run after merge backfills 0.9.0 and has never been exercised.
Workflows only use macos-latest (two Darwin rows in the release build matrix); it resolves to macOS 26 arm64, and x86_64 is cross-compiled, so the macOS 14 retirement doesn't affect the repo.
CI for the stacked PRs: actionlint and zizmor --offline are the workflow checks; typos and oxfmt --check are used for changed files.

code.finding: RELEASE_COORDINATOR_WORKFLOW_PATH = ".github/workflows/callisto-release.yml" is hard-coded in Callisto 0.16.0 and determines the required attesting workflow filename.
Documents that the Homebrew tap's `brew bump` finds the npm/caliper-docgen@x.y.z tag via livecheck and builds from source.

workflow: Stacked PRs merged top-down or into a parent branch after the parent already landed on main strand their commits; merge bottom-up, or retarget to main, and verify content reached main afterward.
Fix stranded commits by merging main into the stranded branches with signed merge commits and opening new PRs against main.
Verify every commit is signed locally (status G) and shows as verified on GitHub before reporting a branch done; the user added a signing key mid-session.
Entire trail descriptions may not render Markdown tables (unverified, docs silent); bullet lists are a safe fallback. Don't state an inferred cause as fact; check docs when challenged.

Sub-agent workers in isolated worktrees committing signed locally without pushing, with the lead pushing and linking via `entire trail link` after review, suits self-contained lineages; the cap is three live sessions.
Link trail branches with `entire trail link <n> --branch <b> --base <parent>` before any PR exists, pushing in stack order.

friction: #281 and #283 merged into parent branches after the parents had already merged to main, stranding their commits and requiring re-landing via #289/#290.
`callisto release pending` failed with E166 on an older release decision that no longer decodes, requiring a pinned --from.
Could not produce an intent with slots locally (`release plan --package` failed with E160), so the artifact-manifest step is copied from Callisto's example and untested.
Entire trail table rendering was uncertain: first stated as unsupported from a screenshot, then docs turned out silent, requiring a corrected memory note.
#287 showed BLOCKED after being retargeted to main and was not diagnosed; its PR body omits the recovery changes merged in from #288.
Branch protection or rulesets referencing release.yml could not be checked from repo contents.
open_items: Watch the in-progress Release & Publish run on main, likely the first 0.9.0 backfill (rebuild, attest, create GitHub Release); it has never run.
Check branch protection/rulesets for the old release.yml filename.
Check the Homebrew tap config for :github_latest, which would see the new Release.
Rehearse the release flow on a scratch repo per docs/releasing.md; the untested pieces are artifact-manifest, gh attestation verify, Windows tar.gz and the schedule trigger.
Decide whether to keep the daily 05:23 UTC schedule, since Callisto's own example has none.
Decide whether to pin macos-26 in the release matrix for deterministic builds.
Merge #289 and #290 so oracle/three-tools-report can start.
Wait for the weekly PRs before starting feat/agent-eval-weekly, which edits weekly.py.
Review, push and link the signed branches from the t155-156-detect and t157-trust workers.
Decide whether to keep #285 for its memory win, and whether to scope a follow-up for trail 154, which missed its 141 ms / 275 MiB goal (about -6% time, -5% memory; antd recall 92.1% vs ~95% target).
Optionally test a table in a trail body to settle Markdown rendering.
No retry added for the E148 race; OIDC trusted publishing deferred because Callisto 0.16.0 doesn't ship it.
